summary: Special Council (June 29, 2026) consolidated major planning and finance decisions: presentations on Parks DCC updates, citywide Design Guidelines, and Environmental DPA mapping. Issued DVP25-0006 to expand the RCMP detachment (698 Atkins Ave. and adjacent properties); Councillor Guiry opposed. Approved the 2025 Statement of Financial Information; staff noted 2025 includes retro firefighter payments and staff increases explaining remuneration rises. Approved the Aquatic Centre supplementary agreement with YMCA/YWCA and directed creation of an Aquatic Centre Reserve Fund and staff to explore expanded youth programming. Gave readings/adopted a package of bylaws: zoning amendments (including new residential zones and small-scale multi-unit housing), OCP amendment to adopt consolidated Design Guidelines and updated EDPA maps, a new Tree Protection Bylaw, and adoption of Amenity Cost Charge and Inclusionary Zoning bylaws.

items.title: PRESENTATIONS
items.plain_english_summary: Three consultant presentations were given: Parks DCC Rates; Design Guidelines; and Environmental Development Permit Guidelines.
items.description: Presentations: (5.1) Proposed Parks DCC Rates; (5.2) Design Guidelines; (5.3) Environmental Development Permit Guidelines. Each included consultant slides and Q&A with Council.
items.debate_summary: Consultants presented draft policy tools: modest increases to Parks DCCs (approx. +5.6%), new/updated citywide design guidelines (consolidation of 21 DPAs to a single citywide design DPA with a recommended Advisory Design Panel), and updated environmental DPA mapping and guidelines emphasizing ecological connectivity and Riparian Areas Protection (RAPR) alignment. Council asked implementation and policy-detail questions and staff explained next steps for consultation and bylaw readings.

key_quotes.text: So the new DCC rates result in a rather modest increase of 5.6% across the board.
key_quotes.speaker: Sean Heffernan

key_quotes.text: This is a single unified set of guidelines that adapts to Langford's diverse landscapes.
key_quotes.speaker: Valeria Perez Malvido

key_statements.statement_text: Staff/consultant recommends modest increases of approximately 5.6% to Parks DCC rates and introduces a new commercial/industrial rate.
key_statements.speaker: Sean Heffernan
key_statements.context: During presentation of proposed Parks DCC Rates (5.1)

key_statements.statement_text: The proposed DCC program uses a 30-year horizon and adds commercial/industrial as a charged category to increase program revenue.
key_statements.speaker: Sean Heffernan

key_statements.statement_text: Consolidate 21 separate DPAs into one citywide Form & Character Design Guideline to provide clarity and consistency for applicants and staff.
key_statements.speaker: Valeria Perez Malvido

key_statements.statement_text: Recommend establishing a limited Advisory Design Panel (ADP) to provide expert design advice and improve consistency of outcomes.
key_statements.speaker: Valeria Perez Malvido

key_statements.statement_text: Update EDPA mapping using LiDAR, SEI and field verification; combine sensitive ecosystems and potential habitat into a refined map and include a 45 m buffer around watercourses to align with RAPR.
key_statements.speaker: Lauren Smith

key_statements.statement_text: Increase the role of Qualified Environmental Professionals (QEPs) and require stronger monitoring and restoration language to reduce cumulative impacts.
key_statements.speaker: Lauren Smith

items.title: Proposed Parks DCC Rates (approx. 30 min)
items.plain_english_summary: Consultant presented draft Parks DCC rates (combined acquisition & improvement) with an approximate 5.6% increase and a new commercial/industrial rate.
items.description: Presentation of draft Parks Development Cost Charge rates: methodology, draft rates, implementation considerations (in-stream protection, assist factor, consultation), and next steps to bring bylaw for readings.
items.debate_summary: Council asked for clarification about project lists, in-stream protection, municipal assist factor, and how acquisition priorities affect rates; the consultant confirmed the small rate increases and explained consultation and timing (ins-stream protected period and potential grace period). Several public speakers later expressed concern about rate increases and municipal spending (during public participation).

key_quotes.text: These are fees and charges that are used to recover the cost of off-site infrastructure required to support growth and development.
key_quotes.speaker: Sean Heffernan

key_quotes.text: The proposed land use categories... include commercial and industrial uses — a new category of charge in the DCC program.
key_quotes.speaker: Sean Heffernan

key_statements.statement_text: The draft Parks DCC rates represent a modest overall increase (~5.6%), consolidating acquisition and improvement into one parks DCC.
key_statements.speaker: Sean Heffernan

key_statements.statement_text: Adding a commercial/industrial park DCC category will increase program revenue compared to current practice (where those uses were not charged).
key_statements.speaker: Sean Heffernan
key_statements.context: Explaining rate structure and new categories

key_statements.statement_text: Council may choose a larger municipal assist factor (above the 1% legislated minimum) to reduce rates, but that requires compensating non-DCC revenue.
key_statements.speaker: Sean Heffernan

items.title: Design Guidelines (approx. 30 min)
items.plain_english_summary: MODUS presented consolidated citywide Form & Character Design Guidelines to replace multiple DPAs, with guidance organized into site planning, architecture, landscape architecture and special considerations.
items.description: Presentation of new consolidated design guidelines: background, consultation, themes/principles (honouring place, building resilience, creating connection, fostering creativity), structure, design & practice examples, and implementation steps including suggested Advisory Design Panel and applicants' fundamentals checklist.
items.debate_summary: Council and staff asked for clarification on number/typology of DPAs, heritage considerations, tree/landscaping expectations, and how the ADP and guidelines will work together with updated zoning; presenters confirmed the guidelines are intended to be flexible, visually explanatory and supported by an implementation toolkit (checklist and ADP recommendations).

key_quotes.text: This update consolidates nearly 1,100 guidelines across 21 DPAs into 75 guidelines in one citywide DPA.
key_quotes.speaker: Valeria Perez Malvido

key_quotes.text: Design guidelines are the bridge between policy and practice.
key_quotes.speaker: Valeria Perez Malvido

key_statements.statement_text: Consolidate existing DPAs into a single citywide DPA (except master-planned areas), reducing duplication and improving clarity for applicants and staff.
key_statements.speaker: Valeria Perez Malvido

key_statements.statement_text: Recommend establishing a scoped Advisory Design Panel to provide expert review for select projects and smooth implementation.
key_statements.speaker: Valeria Perez Malvido

key_statements.statement_text: Guidelines focus on human-scaled public realm, integrating nature, and promoting authentic, context-driven design rather than a single stylistic approach.
key_statements.speaker: Valeria Perez Malvido

items.title: Environmental Development Permit Guidelines (approx. 30 min)
items.plain_english_summary: DiamondHead Consulting presented updated Environmental DPA mapping, reduced mapping layers (from three to two DPAs), stronger EDPA guidelines, and added emphasis on ecological connectivity and RAPR alignment.
items.description: Presentation covered scope, field verification using LiDAR & SEI, 54 field plots, proposed changes (sensitive ecosystems DPA + riparian DPA with a 45 m buffer), expanded QEP role, monitoring and restoration requirements, and clarified exemptions.
items.debate_summary: Consultant explained the data-driven mapping updates (LiDAR, field verification) and new emphasis on connectivity and QEP-led assessments; Council questioned how culverted/lost streams are handled and how restorations or daylighting might be pursued — consultant explained provincial approvals and that EDPA flags the need for provincial/regulatory processes (e.g., RAPR).

key_quotes.text: A 45-metre buffer was applied to the water courses ... to be inclusive of the measures to protect the SPA as designated by RAPR.
key_quotes.speaker: Lauren Smith

key_statements.statement_text: Refine EDPA mapping using LiDAR, SEI, and field verification; combine sensitive ecosystems and potential habitat into a single refined map.
key_statements.speaker: Lauren Smith

key_statements.statement_text: Introduce a 45 m buffer around confirmed watercourses to capture RAPR assessment areas and protect SPAs.
key_statements.speaker: Lauren Smith

key_statements.statement_text: Require stronger guidance to QEPs and monitoring during construction to reduce cumulative impacts and better protect connectivity.
key_statements.speaker: Lauren Smith

items.title: Langford Aquatic Centre - Supplementary Agreement with YMCA

items.description: Approve the Aquatic Centre Supplementary Agreement substantially in the form attached; direct staff to explore expanded youth (grades 6–12) programming with the YMCA/YWCA; direct staff to bring forward bylaws/documents to establish an Aquatic Centre Management Reserve Fund to hold funds contributed under the Agreement for facility-related use.
items.debate_summary: Council approved the supplementary agreement and directed staff to work with YMCA/YWCA to explore expanded programming (motion included direction to investigate youth programming and to create a reserve fund to hold facility-related funds); Council and public asked about operational deficits and long-term lifecycle costs identified during acquisition due diligence.

key_quotes.text: If the YMCA/YWCA generates a surplus, those funds will remain tied to the aquatic centre to be used for either facility-related reserve needs or for programming and services.
key_quotes.speaker: Staff Report / Speaker_15

key_statements.statement_text: Approve the Aquatic Centre Supplementary Agreement and authorize the Mayor and CAO or Corporate Officer to execute; surplus funds generated by the operator remain tied to the facility for facility/reserve or programming use.
key_statements.speaker: C. Harder (mover)

key_statements.statement_text: Direct staff to work with YMCA/YWCA to explore expanding recreation opportunities with a focus on programming for youth grades 6–12.
key_statements.speaker: C. Harder (motion amendment/direction)

motions.motion_text: THAT Council approve the Aquatic Centre Supplementary Agreement between the City and the YMCA/YWCA, substantially in the form attached; THAT Council direct staff to work with the YMCA/YWCA to explore expanding recreational opportunities at the Langford Aquatic Centre with a focus on programming for youth in grades six through twelve; AND THAT Council direct staff to bring forward all necessary bylaws and related documents to establish the City's Aquatic Centre Management Reserve Fund for the purpose of receiving and holding funds contributed pursuant to the Supplementary Agreement.
motions.plain_english_summary: Council approved the Aquatic Centre supplementary agreement, directed staff to explore youth programming, and to create the Aquatic Centre Reserve Fund.

items.title: BYLAW NOS. 2274 & 2273 - New Residential Zones & Small-scale Multi-Unit Housing (Adoption)
items.matter_title: Langford Zoning Bylaw No. 300, Amendment No. 761 (New Residential Zones) & Amendment No. 760 (Small Scale Multi Unit Housing)
items.plain_english_summary: Council adopted the zoning amendments: Omnibus No. 68 - New Residential Zones (Bylaw 2274) and Small Scale Multi Unit Housing (Bylaw 2273).
items.description: Adoption of two zoning bylaw amendments to implement new residential zones and small-scale multi-unit housing regulations.
items.debate_summary: Council adopted both zoning bylaws (new residential zones and small-scale multi-unit housing) to implement updated zoning and live landscaping requirements; staff explained how these interact with design guidelines.

motions.motion_text: THAT Council adopt 'Langford Zoning Bylaw No. 300, Amendment No. 761 (Omnibus No. 68 - New Residential Zones), Bylaw No. 2274, 2026' AND THAT Council adopt 'Langford Zoning Bylaw No. 300, Amendment No. 760 (Small Scale Multi Unit Housing), Bylaw No. 2273, 2026'.
motions.plain_english_summary: Adopted zoning amendments for new residential zones and small-scale multi-unit housing.

items.title: BYLAW NOS. 2275, 2270 & 2271 - Amenity Cost Charge; Inclusionary Zoning; Reserve Fund Amendment (Adoption)
items.matter_title: City of Langford Amenity Cost Charge Bylaw No. 2275, 2026; City of Langford Inclusionary Zoning Bylaw No. 2270, 2026; City of Langford Reserve Funds Establishment Bylaw 2004, Bylaw No. 857, Amendment No. 3, Bylaw No. 2271, 2026
items.plain_english_summary: Council adopted the Amenity Cost Charge Bylaw, Inclusionary Zoning Bylaw, and Reserve Funds Establishment Bylaw amendment.
items.description: Adoption of Amenity Cost Charge (ACC) bylaw (for community amenities), Inclusionary Zoning bylaw (affordable housing requirements), and amendment to the Reserve Funds Establishment bylaw to create/authorize associated reserve funds.
items.debate_summary: Council adopted ACC and Inclusionary Zoning bylaws to require amenities and affordable housing contributions; staff and Council noted these are key tools to secure community amenities and affordable units as development occurs.

key_statements.statement_text: Adoption of the Amenity Cost Charge and Inclusionary Zoning bylaws provides tools to collect developer contributions for community amenities and affordable housing.
key_statements.speaker: K. Yacucha (mover)

motions.motion_text: THAT Council adopt Amenity Cost Charge Bylaw No. 2275, 2026; AND THAT Council adopt Inclusionary Zoning Bylaw No. 2270, 2026; AND THAT Council adopt City of Langford Reserve Funds Establishment Bylaw, 2004, Bylaw No. 857, Amendment No. 3, Bylaw No. 2271, 2026.
motions.plain_english_summary: Adopt ACC, Inclusionary Zoning, and Reserve Fund amendment bylaws.

items.title: IN CAMERA RESOLUTION
items.plain_english_summary: Council moved to close the meeting to the public under sections 90(1)(e) and 90(2)(b) of the Community Charter to discuss land acquisition/disposition and confidential negotiations.
items.description: Motion to close the meeting pursuant to Community Charter provisions for land negotiations and intergovernmental/third-party confidential matters.
items.debate_summary: Council moved to close the meeting to consider confidential matters relating to land acquisition/disposition and negotiation information; motion carried.

motions.motion_text: THAT Council close the meeting to the public pursuant to section 90 (1)(e) and (2)(b) of the Community Charter to consider the acquisition, disposition or expropriation of land or improvements and the consideration of information received and held in confidence related to negotiations.
motions.plain_english_summary: Close meeting to public for confidential land/negotiation matters.

items.title: ADJOURNMENT
items.plain_english_summary: Council adjourned the meeting.
items.description: Motion to adjourn the meeting.
